rules.statement: Public functions and methods MUST have unique UUID identifiers for Knowledge Graph synchronization.
rules.rationale: Downgraded to support A3 loop throughput. Finalizer handles assignment.

rules.statement: Symbol identifiers (# ID:) MUST be globally unique across the entire codebase.

A '# ID:' anchor MUST sit on the line immediately before the def, async def, or class it identifies. An anchor that annotates no symbol is a defect; the identity MUST be re-attached to its symbol, never regenerated.
rules.rationale: The inverse of linkage.assign_ids, which asks whether each public symbol has an anchor and so never inspects anchors on private symbols or stray file-level anchors. An anchor split from its def (by a blank line or an inserted method) is valid Python -- ruff and mypy cannot see it -- and the only code that noticed was the cleanup phase of fix.ids, which deletes it: the identity is lost, and the deletion lands in whatever commit the autonomous remediator makes next (9e9067eb, 2026-09-16: a stray anchor was swept into an unrelated consequence-chain commit). Detection is stateless (ast_gate, shared.ast_utility.find_orphan_id_lines -- the same definition fix.ids uses), so it runs in the offline CI gate. Deliberately not auto-remediated: fix.ids strips orphans, and stripping is the wrong remedy for a rule whose point is identity preservation.
